extracted.intended_audience: Users of the computer algebra system SINGULAR (computational algebraists / mathematicians implementing or using desingularization and auxiliary libraries)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for procedures in SINGULAR libraries (resbinomial.lib, resgraph.lib, resjung.lib, resolve.lib) describing usage, inputs, outputs, notes and examples for algorithms used in resolution/desingularization and related utilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: elimrep
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: elimrep(L); L is a list. Compute: Eliminate repeated terms from a list. Return: the same list without repeated terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided: elimrep on list L=4,5,2,5,7,8,6,3,2 returns 4,5,2,7,8,6,3. (From resbinomial.lib.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Emaxcont
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: Emaxcont(Coef,Exp,k,n,flag); Coef,Exp,flag lists, k,n integers. Compute: Identify ALL the variables of E-maximal contact. Return: a list with the indexes of the variables of E-maximal contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show calling Emaxcont on data(J,...) and checking hyp[1] for max E-order and hyp[2] for hypersurfaces of E-maximal contact; note: messages such as 'E-order zero!' may appear and behaviour depends on ring and ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: cleanunit
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute: Clean (or forget) the units in a monomial, given by 'y' variables. Return: The list defining the monomial ideal already cleaned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage shown via cleanunit(L[2][1][1],4,flag) where L[2][1][1] is exponent list; example transforms exponents [3,1,5,8] to [3,0,5,0] removing unit-exponents corresponding to y-variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: resfunction
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: resfunction(invariant,auxinv,nchart,n); invariant, auxinv lists, nchart, n integers. Compute: Patch the resolution function. Return: The complete resolution function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: resfunction(L[3],L[7],7,2) completes an 'incomplete resolution function' L[3]; returns a list representing the resolution function entries. Used with output of Eresol.

rubrics_metrics.name: calculateI
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: calculateI(Coef,expJ,c,n,Y,a,b,D); Coef, expJ, D lists, c, b numbers, n,Y integers, a intvec. Return: ideal I, non monomial part of J.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows using calculateI after blowing up and selecting charts; returns ideal data for non-monomial part in given chart. Used within resbinomial.lib resolution steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maxord
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: Maxord(L,n); L list, n integer. Compute: Find the maximal entry of a list, input is a list defining a monomial. Return: maximum entry of a list and its position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Maxord on exponent list of x(1)^2*x(2)*x(3)^5 returns '5 3' (value 5 at position 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gamma
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: Gamma(L,c,n); L list, c number, n integer. Compute: The Gamma function, resolution function corresponding to the monomial case. Return: lists of maximum exponents in L, value of Gamma function, center of blow up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Gamma on exponents of x(1)^2*x(2)*x(3)^5*x(4)^2*x(5)^3 with c=9 returns maximum exponents, maximal Gamma value (10/9 in example), and center indices [3,5,4].

rubrics_metrics.name: convertdata
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: convertdata(C,L,n,flaglist); C, L, flaglist lists, n integer. Compute: Compute the ideal corresponding to the given lists C,L. Return: an ideal whose coefficients are given by C, exponents given by L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example reconstructs an ideal J2 from lists L[1] (coefficients) and L[2] (exponents); returns ideal entries matching original polynomial data. Useful for data ⇄ ideal conversions.

rubrics_metrics.name: lcmofall
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: lcmofall(nchart,mobile); nchart integer, mobile list of lists. Compute: Compute the lcm of the denominators of the E-orders of all the charts. Return: an integer given the lcm. Note: CALL BEFORE salida.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: For an 8-chart decomposition with rational exponents, lcmofall returns 2. Used to unify denominators across charts.

rubrics_metrics.name: computemcm
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: computemcm(Eolist); Eolist list. Return: an integer, the least common multiple of the denominators of the E-orders (for one chart).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Similar to lcmofall but for one chart; necessary because E-orders are of type number. Example returns 2 for a chart with E-orders 3 and 9/2.

rubrics_metrics.name: constructH
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: constructH(Hhist,n,flag); Hhist intvec, n integer, flag list. Return: the list of exceptional divisors accumulated at this chart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: constructH on history vector returns a list of exceptional divisors like [x(3), x(1), ...]. Used to build the exceptional divisor list from blow-up history.

rubrics_metrics.name: constructblwup
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: constructblwup(blwhist,n,chy,flag); blwhist, flag lists, n integer, chy ideal. Return: the ideal defining the map K[W] -> K[Wi], which gives the composition map of all the blowing up leading to this chart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: NECESSARY START WITH COLUMNS. Example: constructblwup returns images such as _[1]=x(1)^3*x(3), _[2]=x(2), _[3]=x(1)^2*x(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: constructlastblwup
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: constructlastblwup(blwhist,n,chy,flag); blwhist, flag lists, n integer, chy ideal. Return: the ideal defining the last blow up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: NECESSARY START WITH COLUMNS. Example: returns maps _[1]=x(1), _[2]=x(2), _[3]=x(1)*x(3) for the last blow up.

rubrics_metrics.name: genoutput
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: genoutput(chart,mobile,nchart,nsons,n,q,p); chart, mobile, nsons lists, nchart, n,q, p integers. Return: two lists, first gives rings corresponding to final charts, second is list of all rings corresponding to affine charts of resolution process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: genoutput used after Eresol(L) and produces human-readable presentation via presentTree(B). It outputs detailed chart data (ambient space, ideal of variety, exceptional divisors, images of original variables). Notes for visualization reference reszeta.lib tools (collectDiv) and ResTree from resgraph.lib.

rubrics_metrics.name: salida
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: salida(idchart,chart,mobile,numson,previousa,n,q,p); idchart, numson, n, q, p integers, chart, mobile, lists, previousa intvec. Compute: Convert the output of a chart into a ring, where a basic object (BO) is defined. Return: the ring corresponding to the chart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: salida returns a ring RR that can be setring and used to inspect BO; examples show BO components and matrices. Often called after genoutput/lcm computations and before analysis of chart ring data.

rubrics_metrics.name: iniD
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: iniD(n); n integer. Return: list of lists of zeros of size n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: iniD(3) returns three zero entries; used to initialize data structures (lists of zeros).

rubrics_metrics.name: sumlist
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sumlist(L1,L2); L1,L2 lists (size(L1)==size(L2)). Return: a list, sum of L1 and L2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: sumlist(1,2,3 , 5,9,7) returns 6,11,10. Basic utility in resbinomial.lib.

rubrics_metrics.name: reslist
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: reslist(L1,L2); L1,L2 lists (size(L1)==size(L2)). Return: a list, subtraction of L1 and L2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: reslist(1,2,3 , 5,9,7) returns -4,-7,-4.

rubrics_metrics.name: multiplylist
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: multiplylist(L,a); L list, a number. Return: list of elements of type number, multiplication of L times a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: multiplylist(1,2,3, 1/5) returns 1/5,2/5,3/5.

rubrics_metrics.name: dividelist
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: dividelist(L1,L2); L1,L2 lists. Return: list of elements of type number, division of L1 by L2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: dividelist(1,2,3 , 5,9,7) returns 1/5,2/9,3/7.

rubrics_metrics.name: createlist
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: createlist(L1,L2); L1,L2 lists (size(L1)==size(L2)). Return: list of lists of two elements, the first one of L1 and the second of L2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: createlist(1,2,3 , 5,9,7) returns list entries pairing 1 with 5, 2 with 9, 3 with 7. Utility to bundle parallel lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: InterDiv
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: InterDiv(M[,name]); M = matrix (first entry of output of 'intersectionDiv' from reszeta.lib). Create: file 'name.jpg' containing dual graph of resolution if filename is given. Note: requires write permission and external programs 'display' (imagemagick) and 'dot' (graphviz) in PATH; only available on UNIX-type systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: nothing (generates graphics output in separate window). Intended for visualization of intersection divisor dual graph.

rubrics_metrics.name: ResTree
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ResTree(L,M[,name][,mark]); L = list (output of 'resolve'), M = matrix (first entry of 'collectDiv(L)'), optional name, optional mark intvec. Create: file 'name.jpg' containing the tree of charts of L. Note: mark controls border colour of boxes (0 black, 1 red). Requires 'display' and 'dot' in PATH; UNIX-only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: nothing (generates graphics output). Example usage includes passing output of resolve and collectDiv; useful to visualize resolution chart tree. Permission and external tools required.

rubrics_metrics.name: finalCharts
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: finalCharts(L1,L2,iv[,name]); L1 = output of 'resolve', L2 = output of 'intersectionDiv(L1)', iv = first entry of output of 'abstractR(L1)'. Create: new windows in which surf-images of the final charts are presented and several '.ras' files in directory if name given. Note: only available on UNIX-type systems; external programs 'surf' and 'display' needed in PATH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: nothing (generates graphics output). Used to view final chart surfaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: jungresolve
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: jungresolve(ideal J[,is_noeth]); J = ideal, is_noeth = int. Assume: J is two-dimensional ideal. Return: a list l of rings; each l[i] is a ring containing two Ideals: QIdeal and BMap; BMap defines a birational morphism from V(QIdeal) -> V(J) such that V(QIdeal) is smooth. If is_noeth=1, algorithm assumes J is in Noether position; otherwise computes a coordinate change (randomized).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: Resolution of surface singularities using Jung algorithm. Example: resolves z^2 - x^3 - y^3 into rings with QIdeal and BMap entries. Performance may vary because Noether position algorithm is randomized.

rubrics_metrics.name: jungnormal
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: jungnormal(ideal J[,is_noeth]); J = ideal. Assume: J is two-dimensional ideal. Return: a list l of rings where each l[i] contains QIdeal and BMap so that V(QIdeal) has only Hirzebruch-Jung singularities. If is_noeth=1 algorithm assumes Noether position, otherwise computes coordinate change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: jungnormal on z^2-x^3-y^3 yields QIdeal and BMap data similar to jungresolve; useful to obtain normal form with Hirzebruch-Jung singularities before further resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: jungfib
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: jungfib(J[,is_noeth]); J = ideal. Assume: J is two-dimensional ideal. Return: list of rings; l[i] contains QIdeal and BMap such that V(QIdeal) has only quasi-ordinary singularities. If is_noeth=1 assumes Noether position, otherwise computes coordinate change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: jungfib on z^2-x^3-y^3 returns QIdeal with quasi-ordinary singularity polynomial and BMap mapping; part of Jung-family of routines.

rubrics_metrics.name: blowUp
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: blowUp(J,C[,W][,E]); W,J,C = ideals, E = list. Assumes: J = ideal containing W (W=0 if not specified), C = ideal containing J, E list of smooth hypersurfaces. Compute: the blowing up of W in C, the exceptional locus, the strict transform of J and the blowup map. Important difference to blowUp2: ambient space V(W) is blown up (V(J) transformed in it) and V(C) is assumed non-singular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: list l of affine rings (one per chart) each containing ideals aS (blown up ambient space), sT (strict transform), eD (exceptional divisor), bM (blowup map) and BO. Example demonstrates retrieving sT, eD, bM from a returned ring. Used in resolve.lib desingularization pipeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: blowUp2
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: blowUp2(J,C); J,C = ideals. Assume: C is ideal containing J. Note differences to blowUp: V(J) itself is blown up (not ambient space) and C is not assumed non-singular. Compute: blowing up of J in C, the exceptional locus and blow-up map.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: list of affine rings (charts) where each contains Jnew (blownup J), eD (new exceptional divisor), bM (blowup map). Example shows two charts with Jnew and eD entries; used when center may be singular.

rubrics_metrics.name: Center
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: Center(J[,W][,E]); J,W = ideals, E = list. Assume: J = ideal containing W (W=0 if not specified), E = list of smooth hypersurfaces. Compute: the center of the blow-up of J for the resolution algorithm of Bravo-Encinas-Villamayor. Return: ideal describing the center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Center(x^2 - y^3) returned ideal [y, x] (i.e., center generated by y and x). Used by resolve algorithm to pick blow-up centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: resolve
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: resolve(J); or resolve(J,i[,k]); J ideal, i,k ints. Compute: a resolution of J using Villamayor algorithm. Debugging flags i combine switches j1..j6 to toggle correctness checks and debug info.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: a list L of two lists of rings: L[1][i] are rings containing basic object BO (result of resolution), L[2] contains all rings occurring during resolution. Note: presentTree() can be used to view result. Example shows using resolve on a sample ideal and inspecting BO via showBO(BO).

rubrics_metrics.name: showBO
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: showBO(BO); BO = basic object (a list: ideal W, ideal J, intvec b, list Ex, ideal ab, intvec v, intvec w, matrix M). Return: nothing, only pretty printing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Function prints ambient space, ideal of variety, exceptional divisors, images of variables, etc. Used to inspect basic object returned by resolve/blowUp/other routines.

rubrics_metrics.name: presentTree
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: presentTree(L); L = list (output of resolve). Return: nothing, only pretty printing of the output data of resolve().
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows human-readable presentation of the resolution tree and chart data. Often used after genoutput or resolve to view full resolution information.

rubrics_metrics.name: showDataTypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: showDataTypes(); Return: nothing, only pretty printing of extended version of help text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displays detailed information on the BO data type and other internal data structures useful for developers or advanced users inspecting returned objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: blowUpBO
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: blowUpBO(BO,C,e); BO = basic object (list with W,J,b,Ex,ab,v,w,M), C = ideal, e = integer (0 usual blowing up, 1 deleting extra charts, 2 deleting no charts). Assume: R = basering, polynomial ring; W an ideal of R, J = ideal containing W, C = ideal containing J. Compute: (documentation truncated here) presumed to perform blow up on a basic object with options for deletions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedure is part of resolve.lib and is used to blow up a basic object along center C; parameter e controls chart deletion behaviour. Full compute/return descriptions continue beyond this chunk.
